content.en: Researchers are exploring the potential of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms in controlling and optimizing fluid mechanics problems. By teaching empirical strategies to artificial neural networks through trial and error, these algorithms can effectively control flow, reduce drag, and optimize sensor placement. They are also being used to develop control strategies for various flow configurations, including laminar and turbulent flows, weakly turbulent conditions, and flows with rotational oscillations. Additionally, DRL algorithms are being applied to reduce skin friction drag, suppress perturbations in convectively unstable flows, and achieve turbulent drag reduction in channel flows.
content.da: Forskere undersøger potentialet i deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algoritmer til at kontrollere og optimere problemer inden for fluidmekanik. Ved at undervise empiriske strategier til kunstige neurale netværk gennem forsøg og fejl kan disse algoritmer effektivt kontrollere strømning, reducere modstand og optimere placeringen af sensorer. De bliver også brugt til at udvikle kontrolstrategier for forskellige strømkonfigurationer, herunder laminar og turbulent strømning, svagt turbulente forhold og strømninger med rotationsoscillationer. Derudover anvendes DRL-algoritmer til at reducere overfladetræk, undertrykke forstyrrelser i konvektivt ustabile strømninger og opnå turbulent modstandsreduktion i kanalstrømninger.

critic.en: What you're describing is a perfect example of the unchecked optimism that some have about AI and digital solutions for everything. But do we really want to rely on algorithms for things as critical as fluid dynamics optimization?
critic.da: Ah, nej! Skal vi virkelig give maskinerne muligheden for at styre vores væsker? Hvad med de gode gamle metoder, hvor vi som mennesker selv havde kontrollen?

potential.en: This sounds like a fantastic application of deep reinforcement learning in solving complex fluid mechanics problems! It's amazing how technology is being leveraged to explore, understand, and control the behavior of fluids. By training artificial neural networks through trial and error, researchers are essentially mimicking the way humans learn and improve, which is a fascinating concept. I can't wait to see how this technology further develops and its potential impact on various industries, such as aeronautics, automotive, and renewable energy.
potential.da: Det er fascinerende, hvordan DRL-algoritmer nu begynder at træde ind på området for strømningsmekanik. Potentialet til at kontrollere og optimere komplekse flowproblemer er enormt. Jeg er især begejstret for anvendelserne i reduktion af drag og optimering af sensorer, da det kan have store konsekvenser for effektivitet og bæredygtighed, især i transportsektoren. Det viser virkelig potentialet, teknologi og digitalisering har til at skabe en bedre og mere effektiv fremtid!
